subtitle: When Silver Spoke of a Fallen King

panels.shot: dramatic top-down close-up of a mound of ancient silver coins half-buried in dark earth, faint twin images pressed into their faces
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) looms as a faint, watchful silhouette above a glittering heap of Nahapana’s overstruck silver coins in a Nashik field, the sky heavy with monsoon clouds.

dialogue.text: In a quiet field near Jogalthambi, thousands of silver voices remember a war of kings: when Gautamiputra Satakarni hammered his name over Nahapana’s, and conquest was struck not on flesh, but on coin.

i18n.hi: जोगलठांबी के सन्नाटे खेत में, हज़ारों चाँदी की आवाज़ें राजाओं की जंग याद करती हैं: जब गौतमिपुत्र सातकर्णि ने नहपान के नाम पर अपना नाम ठोक दिया, और फतह खाल पर नहीं, सिक्के पर दर्ज हुई।

panels.shot: slow push-in from a wide rural landscape to a small mound in a ploughed field
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) hovers low over a Nashik countryside of tilled fields and scattered trees, focusing on a slight rise in the soil where faint glints of silver peek through.

dialogue.text: Centuries after the Satavahana drums fell silent, a farmer’s plough scraped against metal in the soil of Jogalthambi, and a hidden treasury of history began to shine again.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन ढोलियाँ थमे कई सदियाँ बाद, नासिक के जोगलठांबी में एक हल मिट्टी के नीचे धातु से अटक गया, और इतिहास का छुपा खज़ाना फिर चमक उठा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of earth being pulled aside by unseen hands, coins spilling out, with the spirit looming in the background
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) gazes intently as unseen hands pull back clods of damp earth and a cascade of ancient silver karshapanas tumbles out, catching the muted light.

dialogue.text: From that Nashik district field poured not jewels, but thousands of worn silver karshapanas, each bearing two stories pressed into one thin disc.

i18n.hi: उस नासिक ज़िले के खेत से गहने नहीं, घिसे-पिटे चाँदी के हज़ारों कर्षापन निकले, हर पतले सिक्के पर दो कहानियाँ एक साथ उभरीं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a single coin, one half-shadowed, showing a head and overlapping legends
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) points ethereally toward a single coin held between unseen fingers, its surface showing Nahapana’s profile faint beneath a sharper, overstruck image and tangled letters.

dialogue.text: On one face, the ghost of Nahapana’s head and Greek letters linger; over them, in bold Prakrit, Gautamiputra Satakarni’s name is hammered like a verdict.

i18n.hi: एक तरफ, नहपान का धुँधला सिर और यूनानी अक्षर टिके हैं; उनके ऊपर, मोटे प्राकृत में गौतमिपुत्र सातकर्णि का नाम हथौड़े की फ़रमान जैसा ठपा है।

panels.shot: wide historical flashback shot, bird’s-eye view over the western Deccan with trade routes etched like glowing lines
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) spreads its arms over a ghostly map of the western Deccan, trade routes glowing between ports and upland markets, tiny caravans and ships moving along them.

dialogue.text: To understand this metal whisper, we must look back: to a Deccan criss-crossed by caravans, ports heavy with Roman amphorae, and two powers vying for the same roads and markets.

i18n.hi: इस धातु की फुसफुसाहट समझने के लिए लौटना होगा उस दक्कन में: जहाँ कारवाँ की रेखाएँ थीं, रोमी मटकों से भरे बंदरगाह, और दो ताकतें एक ही राहों और बाज़ारों पर झगड़ती थीं।

panels.shot: low-angle view of a stylised Nahapana on a throne, his coins pouring like a river before him
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) stands off to the side as a regal Nahapana sits on a raised throne in a western kshatrapa court, attendants nearby, a flowing pile of freshly struck silver coins spilling across the floor.

dialogue.text: Nahapana of the Kshaharata line, a ‘kshatrapa’ under greater Saka lords, filled the western Deccan with his silver, his titles circling his portrait in Greek and Brahmi alike.

i18n.hi: क्षहरात वंश का नहपान, बड़े शक शासकों के अधीन ‘क्षत्रप’, अपने चाँदी के सिक्कों से पश्चिमी दक्कन भर देता है, यूनानी और ब्राह्मी दोनों में उसके ख़िताब उसके चित्र के चारों तरफ घूमते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a cave-like assembly, with monks and donors, a scroll laid out showing Ushavadata’s grant
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) watches over a scene inside a rock-cut hall where Ushavadata, Nahapana’s son-in-law, gestures toward a document as monks and local elites look on near carved pillars.

dialogue.text: His son-in-law Ushavadata inscribed his generosity into stone at Nashik and beyond, gifting land and caves, stitching Saka power into the very rock of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: उसका जामाता उषवदात नासिक से आगे तक पत्थरों पर अपनी दानशीलता खुदवाता है, ज़मीन और गुफाएँ बाँटता है, शक सत्ता को दक्कन की चट्टानों में ही सीं देता है।

panels.shot: wide split-scene shot showing Satavahana court on one side, Nahapana’s domain on the other, with overlapping spheres
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) hovers between two half-scenes: on one side a Satavahana court with Brahmin advisers; on the other, Nahapana’s kshatrapa court, their territorial boundaries overlapping like translucent circles.

dialogue.text: Yet to the east, Satavahana kings claimed the same lands, the same merchants, the same river valleys; the stage was set for a struggle that would not only redraw maps, but recast money itself.

i18n.hi: लेकिन पूरब में सातवाहन राजा वही ज़मीन, वही व्यापारी, वही नदी घाटियाँ अपना बताते हैं; मंच तैयार है ऐसे संघर्ष का जो सिर्फ़ नक्शे नहीं, खुद मुद्रा को भी नया रूप देगा।

panels.shot: evocative montage shot: Satavahana warriors advancing, forts changing hands, but seen as shadows on coin surfaces
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) looks down at a spread of coins whose surfaces flicker with shadowy images of marching Satavahana troops, fortified towns, and retreating Saka garrisons, as if wars are reflected in the metal.

dialogue.text: We do not have battle roll calls or dates carved in stone; instead, we have hints— Satavahana gains, Kshaharata retreats— and, above all, this one stubborn hoard of silver.

i18n.hi: हमारे पास न तो युद्ध की सूचियाँ हैं, न तारीख़ें पत्थर पर खुदी; बस इशारे हैं— सातवाहन बढ़त, क्षहरात पीछे हटना— और सबसे बढ़कर, यह ज़िद्दी चाँदी का एक ही ख़ज़ाना।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Satavahana mint scene, workers overstriking older coins under watchful officials
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) stands in a Satavahana mint courtyard as workers place Nahapana’s coins on anvils and strike them with new dies, officials observing with stern focus.

dialogue.text: At some point between the later first and early second century CE, a Satavahana mint received piles of Nahapana’s silver and a clear order: do not melt; overstrike.

i18n.hi: पहली सदी के उत्तरार्ध और दूसरी सदी की शुरुआत के बीच, किसी सातवाहन टकसाल में नहपान के चाँदी के ढेर पहुँचे और साफ़ हुक्म आया: गलाओ मत; ऊपर से ठोक दो।

panels.shot: extreme close-up sequence of a die descending onto a coin, frozen just before impact
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) leans close as a heavy die, engraved with ‘Gautamiputra Satakarni’ in Brahmi, hangs poised above a worn Nahapana coin resting on an anvil.

dialogue.speaker: the_jogalthambi_hoard
dialogue.text: One blow, and an old ruler’s face becomes the pedestal for another’s name.

i18n.hi: एक चोट, और पुराने शासक का चेहरा दूसरे के नाम का चबूतरा बन जाता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of mounds of overstruck coins being stacked and recorded, mint workers exhausted
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) surveys rows of mint workers stacking thousands of freshly overstruck coins into baskets, scribes tallying counts on palm-leaf records nearby.

dialogue.text: Thousands upon thousands passed under the hammer. Scholars debate whether eight, ten, or thirteen thousand; the exact count is blurred, but the sheer scale is not.

i18n.hi: हज़ारों पर हज़ार सिक्के हथौड़े के नीचे गए। विद्वान बहस करते हैं आठ, दस या तेरह हज़ार पर; गिनती धुँधली है, पर पैमाना नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up of an overstruck coin showing both legends readable in parts
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) cradles a coin in its ethereal palm, the faint outline of Nahapana’s Greek legend visible beneath the bolder Prakrit inscription of Gautamiputra Satakarni.

dialogue.text: Rapson’s careful eyes in 1908 traced these layers: the Kshaharata legend underneath, the Satavahana legend above, two regimes compressed into a single, stubborn piece of silver.

i18n.hi: १९०८ में रैप्सन की तेज़ नज़र ने ये परतें पकड़ीं: नीचे क्षहरात की लिखत, ऊपर सातवाहन की, दो राज एक ही ज़िद्दी चाँदी के टुकड़े में दबे हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot in a shaded study, a modern scholar examining Jogalthambi coins under a lens while the spirit watches
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) stands behind a modern numismatist at a desk, as the scholar peers through a magnifying glass at a Jogalthambi coin, notes and reference books scattered around.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars, from Rapson to Bhandare, have turned these pieces over and over, measuring dies, reading worn Brahmi, weighing each coin for clues to sequence and scale.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान, रैप्सन से भंडारे तक, इन सिक्कों को बार–बार पलटते हैं, टकसाल की मुहरें नापते हैं, घिसी ब्राह्मी पढ़ते हैं, हर सिक्के का वज़न तौलकर क्रम और पैमाने के सुराग ढूँढते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nashik Cave 3 interior with inscription panel highlighted, the spirit indicating it
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) stands before the rock wall of Nashik Cave 3, gesturing toward the long inscription panel carved near the entrance as soft light filters in.

dialogue.text: At Nashik Cave 3, an inscription praises Gautamiputra Satakarni for rooting out the Kshaharatas and mentions a grant involving a field once linked to Ushavadata’s gifts, echoing the reversal etched on the coins.

i18n.hi: नासिक गुफा ३ की एक शिला लेख गौतमिपुत्र सातकर्णि की क्षहरातों को उखाड़ फेंकने की प्रशंसा करती है और उस खेत के दान का ज़िक्र करती है जो कभी उषवदात के उपहारों से जुड़ा था, सिक्कों पर खुदे उलटफेर की गूँज जैसी।

panels.shot: medium shot juxtaposing a rubbing of the inscription with a spread of Jogalthambi coins
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) places a parchment rubbing of the Nashik inscription beside a neat array of Jogalthambi overstruck coins on a table, aligning text and metal.

dialogue.text: Text and silver speak in chorus: the prashasti boasts of Kshaharatas uprooted; the overstrikes show their monetary roots cut and grafted into Satavahana stock.

i18n.hi: शब्द और चाँदी एक साथ बोलते हैं: प्रशस्ति क्षहरातों के उन्मूलन का ढोल पीटती है; ओवरस्ट्राइक दिखाते हैं कि उनकी मौद्रिक जड़ें काटकर सातवाहन तने में जोड़ दी गईं।

panels.shot: reflective shot of the spirit between two shadowy figures labeled in style only by crowns: Nahapana and Gautamiputra
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) stands between two semi-transparent figures—one in Saka garb representing Nahapana, the other in Satavahana attire representing Gautamiputra—both fading toward the coin in its hands.

dialogue.text: But the hoard stays silent on what chroniclers love to fix: the exact year Nahapana fell, whether he died in battle or retired, how long Gautamiputra’s triumph lasted in these western tracts.

i18n.hi: पर यह ख़ज़ाना उन बातों पर चुप है जिन्हें इतिहासकार दर्ज करना पसंद करते हैं: नहपान के गिरने का साल, वह जंग में मरा या संन्यास लिया, और गौतमिपुत्र की यह पश्चिमी जीत कितने समय टिकी।

panels.shot: close-up on the spirit’s thoughtful face, coins reflecting shifting dates and scholarly notes
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) gazes thoughtfully at the shimmering coins in its hands, their surfaces briefly reflecting floating numbers and fragments of scholarly debate before settling back into plain silver.

dialogue.text: Some place the overstrikes around 78 CE, others closer to 124 CE; the hoard refuses to pin its tale to a single calendar line, offering sequence and scale instead of tidy dates.

i18n.hi: कुछ इन ओवरस्ट्राइक को ७८ ई. के आस–पास रखते हैं, कुछ १२४ ई. के क़रीब; ख़ज़ाना अपनी कहानी को किसी एक साल से बाँधने से इनकार करता है, साफ़ तारीख़ों की जगह क्रम और पैमाना देता है।

panels.shot: wide present-day village shot, children playing near the field where the hoard once lay, the spirit watching quietly
panels.action: Jogalthambi Hoard (Coin-Hoard Spirit) stands at the edge of the Jogalthambi field in the present day, watching children run and play where the buried hoard once lay unseen.

dialogue.text: Today the field is just earth again, but the Jogalthambi hoard reminds us that power often writes its boldest lines on coin, and that even a worn piece of silver can outlast the empires that struck it.

i18n.hi: आज वह खेत फिर बस मिट्टी है, पर जोगलठांबी का यह ख़ज़ाना याद दिलाता है कि सत्ता अपने सबसे मोटे अक्षर सिक्कों पर लिखती है, और घिसी हुई चाँदी भी उसे गढ़ने वाली साम्राज्यों से ज़्यादा जी सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Silver Spoke of a Fallen King
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब चाँदी ने गिरे राजा की कहानी कही
